title: Budgeted inference options - Summitcrest Wares intake
summary: Initial discovery focused on per-token economics, batching and KV caching tradeoffs, and hosting choices (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer has strict monthly budget caps for Q4 pilot and strong data residency / audit requirements. Next steps: share targeted cost model spreadsheet, schedule 1-hr technical pilot planning with infra and security, run a short latency/throughput bench against their 2k qps synthetic workload.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-08-02 15:00 PST / Duration 48m
Attendees: Aisha Rahman (Redwood AE), Luca Moretti (Redwood SE), Rachel Kim (Summitcrest Head of ML), Daniel Ortega (CTO), Priya Singh (Platform Eng)

Summary (auto): Quick intro, ask about current stack and budget, dive into per-token math, discuss KV cache and batching levers, residency and SOC2 notes, next steps and owners.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Aisha): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh this is Aisha from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We also have Luca our solutions engineer. Could you — can you each intro quickly?
00:10 Rachel (Summitcrest): Yeah hi I'm Rachel, head of ML at Summitcrest Wares. We run recommender and chat-style product assistant for e-comm, around 60M monthly active users.
00:18 Daniel: Daniel, CTO. I'm mostly here for the infra constraints and budget guardrails.
00:22 Priya: Priya, platform eng, I look after networking and our VPCs.
00:26 Aisha: Great — cool. Quick agenda; we want to understand your cost constraints, the workloads you care about, and then Luca will walk through batching/caching levers and deployment options.
00:36 Rachel: Sounds good, thanks.

02:05 Luca (SE): Okay so a couple quick clarifying questions before we jump into numbers. What kind of avg request sizes are you seeing for the assistant versus recommender? Token counts?
02:14 Rachel: For the assistant, average prompt + completion is around 220 tokens. Recommender is shorter, usually 40-60 tokens. The assistant is our expensive call — about 70% of the inference spend.
02:26 Luca: Got it. And throughput expectations for a pilot? Peak QPS?
02:31 Daniel: For pilot we can cap to 2k qps synthetic across a handful of routes, but production peak can be 8-10k later. For now pilot budget is hard capped at $15k for month.
02:44 Aisha: Cool, that budget number is super helpful. One thing we'll do is map per-token cost across hosted vs dedicated vs private and show where batching and KV caching moves the needle.

05:00 Luca: Alright rough sketch — hosted API per-token rates vary by model family and size; for example for a 13B open weight it might be X cents per 1k tokens baseline, but with batching and prefix KV caching you can reduce effective per-request cost significantly. Two levers: batch-level compute amortization and reuse from KV cache for repeated prefixes.
05:22 Priya: When you say KV cache can you explain — we currently have session pins for users, will that map?
05:28 Luca: Yeah, so KV cache is essentially the saved key-value states across generation steps. If you have repeated prefixes or re-used system prompts, KV cache avoids recomputing earlier tokens. In practical terms, if 40% of tokens are repeated, you could see 20-35% token cost reduction depending on model and runtime.
05:45 Rachel: Mm-hmm. Is that automatic on hosted? Or do we need dedicated?
05:50 Luca: On Redwood hosted, the runtime does prefix caching automatically for common patterns; on dedicated/private you have more control and persistence window — that's where residency and long-lived sessions help. The caching behavior depends on model variant and sequence lengths.

08:12 Daniel: Our concern is budget predictability. If we spin up hosted for pilot at $15k, what are realistic throughput & latency tradeoffs? I don't want a surprise bill.
08:22 Aisha: Totally — predictable unit-econ is one of our focuses. We'll propose a model: take your traffic mix (assistant vs reco), apply expected batching factor (we'll estimate from your QPS and typical latency SLO), and then compute per-token cost for hosted and for a Dedicated reserved pool amortized monthly. For 2k qps pilot we can show a hosted path that fits $15k or a small Dedicated slot.

10:40 Luca: Quick example math (ballpark): if assistant has 220 tokens and recommender 50 tokens, weighted avg token per request ~170. At 2k qps that's 2k * 170 * 3600 * 24 * 30 tokens/month — it's a lot, but we break it down to per-request cost. Batching helps because if you can batch small requests into groups of N on GPU, per-token compute reduces. For low-latency SLOs (under 200ms) batching factor is small, maybe 1.2-1.5; if SLO can be looser (500-800ms) we might batch up to 4-6x.
11:15 Rachel: We need <250ms p95 for the chat assistant or UX suffers. So we can't push batch windows too long.
11:22 Luca: Right — so expect modest batching (1.3-1.6x) for that route. But for recommender calls we can go more aggressive. The other trick is routing different routes to different hosting tiers (hosted cheap model for reco, dedicated for assistant).

14:35 Priya: On Private deployment — our security team wants customer-managed KMS, HSM integration and full audit logs retained for a year. Is that supported?
14:45 Aisha: Yes, Private deployments support KMS/HSM and extended audit log retention. Our Private plan also gives you a customer control plane inside your VPC so data never leaves your network. There's a platform fee and support contract; we'll include that price band in the spreadsheet.
14:58 Daniel: SOC2 compliance?
15:02 Aisha: Redwood is SOC2 Type II — we'll attach the report and the security brief. We'll also include SSO/SAML and RBAC details.

18:10 Luca: Back to cost levers — quantization is significant. Moving from FP16 to 4-bit/8-bit quantized weights can reduce GPU RAM and allow denser packing which lowers hourly GPU cost. For many models, quality is preserved with recommended quantization profiles. We'll give specific recs for the models you'd pick.
18:28 Rachel: Are there tradeoffs in latency with quantization?
18:32 Luca: Minimal in our runtime — often sub-5% latency change, sometimes improvement due to cache sizes fitting better. But we'll validate on their traces.

21:05 Daniel: For clarity — what would a Dedicated commitment look like for 2k qps pilot?
21:12 Aisha: For a reserved Dedicated capacity we can propose a month-long committed slot sized for your peak pilot throughput. It has a fixed monthly fee which you can amortize across the token volume; this improves predictability versus hosted. We'll model both.
21:30 Priya: If we go Dedicated but want to keep keys on our KMS, is that a problem?
21:36 Luca: No — Dedicated supports KMS integrations and VPC peering or direct connect. The main difference is you manage the sizing and autoscaling policy with our tooling.

24:00 Rachel: One operational question — retry/misprediction cost. We have lots of short retries from client side, how do we avoid paying for those?
24:09 Luca: Good question. You can use an edge-layer filter to dedupe or shadow requests; Redwood's routing can also gate obvious retries and support idempotency keys. We can show patterns. That alone can cut 5-8% off headline token bill in some apps.

26:30 Aisha: We're going to send a cost-model workbook where you can paste your actual traffic and we'll compute hosted vs dedicated vs private scenarios, with toggles for batching factor, KV cache hit rate, quantization profile, and latency SLO.
26:45 Rachel: Awesome. Will that include a recommended pilot size?
26:49 Aisha: Yep — we'll recommend a pilot that fits your $15k cap and propose guardrails (burst caps, soft limits).

29:20 Priya: Any hidden network egress costs with Private?
29:26 Luca: If everything stays inside the VPC and you keep models in-region, egress is minimal. The main cost is the infra for the model store and storage. We'll itemize those.

31:10 Daniel: I want to understand worst-case — if we hit a traffic spike and fallback occurs, do you have automatic model fallback policies to cheaper variants?
31:20 Luca: Yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible cheaper model or to a cached response. Can set per-route fallback rules and degraded SLOs. That prevents cost blowouts.
31:33 Rachel: Could you give an example of the downgrade path?
31:37 Luca: Sure — assistant primary is 13B float, fallback could be 7B quantized or a shorter-generation policy with a safety summary. We'll put examples in the doc.

35:00 Aisha: Quick reconfirmation of stakeholders and timelines — Rachel leads ML and will own pilot success criteria; Daniel will sign off infra changes; Priya will coordinate sandbox networking. Pilot timeline target: start benchmarks second week of August, 2-week technical pilot then expand. Does that sound feasible?
35:17 Rachel: Yes that fits.

37:40 Priya: For the pilot we'll need a short list of artifacts to prepare.
37:46 Luca: I'll send a bench plan: sample traces, expected qps distribution, sample prompts, and a script to replay traffic. Also a brief infra checklist for VPC peering and KMS creds (if Private/Dedicated).

40:10 Daniel: How do you measure token accounting for charging — do you count prompt+completion or just generated tokens?
40:17 Aisha: We bill on prompt + completion tokens. We also provide per-token breakdowns in the console so you can see which route is driving cost.
40:26 Rachel: Okay good. One more question — latency SLOs if we pin to Dedicated; are there stricter guarantees?
40:33 Aisha: Dedicated has SLA-backed latency targets and reserved GPU throughput. Hosted is best-effort but we publish performance profiles. We'll include percentile latency numbers across models.

44:00 Aisha: Wrap up — recap next steps and owners. We'll send: cost model workbook, security brief and SOC2, benchmarking plan. Luca will draft bench details. Rachel to confirm pilot stakeholders. We'll aim to reconvene after benchmarks.
44:20 Rachel: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
44:25 Daniel: Thanks all.
44:30 Priya: Thanks.

End of transcript.
